research_scope: Previously uncovered base-game Super Skills selected after duplicate checking the canonical repository and prior curated research. Acquisition routes were reconciled against current Xenoverse 2 references rather than inheriting Xenoverse 1 PQ numbering.

verification_audit.method: Selected records were checked against the repository for duplicate names before research. Current Xenoverse 2 skill references were used to reconcile classification, acquisition, resource cost, users, and documented mechanics. Older Xenoverse 1 reward tables were not used as current Xenoverse 2 acquisition evidence.
verification_audit.numbering_warning: Several older guides use Xenoverse 1 Parallel Quest numbering. Current Xenoverse 2 acquisition routes were therefore taken from Xenoverse 2-specific references where available.

records.name: Charge
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 83 — Dangerous Duo! Warriors Never Rest; skill reward
records.skill_description: Jump high, then dive and charge at the opponent with a three-part rushing strike.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 skill data classifies Charge as a Strike Super with a three-hit, tracking, short-range attack. At very close range all three attack portions can connect. The current reference identifies PQ83 as the acquisition source.
records.combo_notes: The move is a short-range rush/strike option; exact combo reliability varies with spacing and target state and is not expanded beyond documented behavior.
records.pve_notes: Provides a straightforward Strike Super for close-range engagements and is associated with Goten's moveset.
records.pvp_notes: Because the move travels through multiple positions, close spacing and target state matter; no universal frame advantage is asserted.

records.name: Stone Bullet
records.unlock_method: Parallel Quest 56 — Hercule Is Number One; random reward
records.skill_description: Throw several rocks in a row; holding the input charges the throw and substantially extends its range.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 references classify Stone Bullet as a Strike Super and document a chargeable projectile. Up to 22 rocks can be thrown in one use, with the charge changing its range. Exact current reward probability is not established and is therefore not supplied.
records.combo_notes: The attack is projectile-like despite its Strike classification; charge level and distance affect practical use.
records.pve_notes: Useful as a ranged harassment option where its chargeable range can be exploited against AI targets.
records.pvp_notes: The unusual Strike classification and chargeable range make spacing important; exact matchup/frame claims remain outside the verified record.

records.name: Double Buster
records.character_source: Trunks (Kid); Future Trunks, Gotenks, Pan, Tapion (Customize Partner where unlocked)
records.unlock_method: Skill Shop after the required story progression; current Xenoverse 2 references identify the shop as the CaC acquisition route
records.skill_description: Fire a two-handed Ki Blast forward; a second input causes the blast to chase the opponent.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 data classifies Double Buster as a Ki Blast Super with a tracking follow-up input. The current skill reference lists the Skill Shop as the acquisition source, superseding older Xenoverse 1 PQ29 reward references for current-game acquisition.
records.combo_notes: The second input changes the projectile trajectory to pursue the target, which is the defining documented mechanic.
records.pve_notes: The tracking follow-up can help against moving AI targets when the initial projectile does not connect.
records.pvp_notes: The additional input can alter projectile tracking, but no universal hit-confirm or frame claim is asserted.

records.name: Finish Buster
records.character_source: Trunks (Future); Trunks (Kid); Pan; Tapion (Customize Partner where unlocked)
records.unlock_method: Skill Shop after the required story progression
records.skill_description: Fire a powerful Ki Blast straight ahead; the user remains exposed during the firing stance.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 references classify Finish Buster as a Ki Blast Super with projectile tracking and long range. The documented current acquisition route is the Skill Shop; older Xenoverse 1 PQ32 references should not be treated as the current Xenoverse 2 unlock route.
records.combo_notes: The move has a long-range projectile profile but leaves the user vulnerable during its firing stance.
records.pve_notes: The long-range projectile can be useful when the AI is already committed or knocked away, while its vulnerability should be accounted for.
records.pvp_notes: The documented vulnerability during the firing stance makes spacing and confirmation important.

records.name: Justice Rush
records.character_source: Videl; Great Saiyaman 2; Pan (Customize Partner where unlocked)
records.skill_description: Release a flurry of punches and kicks, with an Ultimate-cancel opportunity before the final kick.
records.mechanics_notes: Current Xenoverse 2 data classifies Justice Rush as a Strike Super with a ten-hit short-range barrage. The documented input can cancel into an Ultimate before the final kick, and the current acquisition route is mentor training with Videl and Adult Gohan.
records.combo_notes: The final-hit cancel is an explicit documented mechanic and should be preserved as a separate combo property rather than inferred from generic Strike behavior.
records.pve_notes: Its multi-hit close-range sequence can be used as a pressure or combo-ending Super when the target is confirmed.
records.pvp_notes: The documented Ultimate-cancel option gives the move a specific combo utility, but exact frame windows are version-sensitive and not asserted.
